newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes to resume Midwest flights.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes to resume Midwest flights.

text.p: Great Lakes Aviation Ltd on Wednesday said it would resume service between Chicago's O'Hare Airport and four other Midwest cities on Wednesday and Thursday.

The company, operating as United Express, is resuming flights between O'Hare and Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan, and Sioux Falls, South Dakota, on Wednesday, June 11. It is resuming service between Chicago and Terre Haute, Indiana, and Mattoon, Illinois, on June 12.
Great Lakes voluntarily suspended all flights May 16 after U.S. Federal Aviation Administration inspectors found it operated "unairworthy aircraft."
The company said in a statement Wednesday that it planned to resume flights to other cities gradually.
The airline also operated as Midway Connection in the Southeast and as Great Lakes Airlines in the Southwest.
United Express provides commuter service in affiliation with UAL Corp.
